notes: The one universe, growing to every name anyone classifies. A declaration, nothing else: the ticker, the class a human declared for it (never inferred), why that class in words meant to hold for years, and what no model can see for the name. No outcome, number, date, tag or parameter lives here; the run records those per record, and whether anything changed since the last run is the baseline diff. The loader is strict: an unknown field is a load error. An entry may declare the SEC filer to read by cik when the ticker map points elsewhere, with the reason in why.

map_cik, 2026-10-03: a ticker is a label an exchange reissues, and SPCX passed from a fund to a company without the entry noticing. Every entry whose ticker is in the ticker map of the Securities and Exchange Commission now declares map_cik, the CIK the map gave on the day a person last confirmed the entry. The fetch compares it with the map on every run and the record is refused, before anything else, when they differ; the entry is then read again by a person and redeclared. It is a guard and is never read for statements, which is what cik is for. The names outside the map, the foreign lines and a few funds, carry none and are not guarded.

scope_codes.build_out: capital spending runs well above depreciation on capacity that is not yet earning, so the free cash flow or the return the model starts from understates the business
scope_codes.rebound_window: the growth window opens on a recovery from a collapse, so the derived starting growth reads the rebound as growth
scope_codes.trough_window: a reset or trough year sits inside the growth window, so the derived starting growth reads the trough
scope_codes.product_transition: a product transition inside the growth window: a franchise in decline or a launch not yet in the statements
scope_codes.goodwill_heavy: acquired goodwill is a large part of invested capital or sits inside the latest earnings, so the return on capital reads the price paid for a business rather than what it earns
scope_codes.acquired_history: acquisitions or a change of ownership inside the window, or one after the latest statements: the filed history is not the business ahead
scope_codes.carve_out_history: a spin-off, carve-out, divestiture or fresh-start accounting inside the window: part of the filed history is another entity's
scope_codes.short_history: the filed history is short or young, so what the model reads as a through-cycle figure is a few years
scope_codes.structural_break: a declared break in the business, so a through-cycle figure may not recur
scope_codes.backward_looking: the through-cycle average looks backward by construction
scope_codes.captive_finance: a captive finance arm: its interest is an operating cost and its debt funds a lending book, and the model reads both as the company's financing
scope_codes.pass_through_balances: balances held for customers, members or managed funds pass through the statements and are not the company's own cash, debt or working capital
scope_codes.one_off_in_window: a one-time charge, write-down or non-operating loss sits inside the window and is read as an operating year
scope_codes.leases_excluded: operating leases are outside the debt definition, so a lease-heavy estate carries less debt here than its obligations imply
scope_codes.vendor_statements: no filed statements are read: they come from the vendor, with fewer years and no tag behind a number
scope_codes.mixed_business: a material part of the business is of another kind than the class's lens reads
scope_codes.market_marks: earnings carry unrealised marks or performance fees that move with markets, which the model reads as a level
scope_codes.investment_book: a large book of investments sits on the balance sheet at values the model does not read
scope_codes.filer_marks: the value rests on the filer's own marks of unquoted assets, recorded and not verified, with losses visible late
scope_codes.policy_dependent: earnings rest on a policy rate, a tax credit or a government agreement that the company does not control
scope_codes.commodity_exposure: part of revenue or cost moves with a commodity price
scope_codes.concentration: a few customers or products carry a large share of revenue
scope_codes.contract_terms: a large cost or revenue share is set by contracts the statements do not separate
scope_codes.balance_sheet: the balance sheet's own shape, heavy debt or negative book equity, limits what the model can read
scope_codes.ownership_structure: the listed line owns only part of the business, counts only part of the shares, or ranks behind other claims
scope_codes.country_basis: the country that chooses the risk premium is not the legal domicile
scope_codes.loss_making: loss-making on the latest filed years
scope_codes.filer_tagging: the filer's own tagging puts a line under an element that means something else, so a field the record reads is not what its name says
